findings.reason: naming reckon/velocity.py lets §3 extend session_usage (or lift its parse to a shared function) for the per-load delta it needs, instead of maintaining duplicate token accounting that has already failed one independent review.
findings.text: docs/research/data/crew-contract-baseline/measure.py, which §3's done-when names as the token measurement instrument and whose bracketing control the §3 review already found broken, opens the transcript store under ~/.claude/projects itself: it walks it, parses assistant `usage` blocks, sums input + cache_creation + cache_read, and carries its own dispatch regex, duplicating velocity.transcript_index (:1318) and velocity.session_usage (:1339); session_usage already deduplicates by message id, splits uncached/cache-creation/cache-read, and excludes sidechain and out-of-window records, so the plan will re-measure and patch a second parallel reader instead of the owner

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the design concentrates the coordinator contract into one core skill (SKILL.md ≤4,000 words, skill plus references ≤12,000) and demotes the remainder to on-demand references, so it reduces surface rather than spreading complexity across small wrappers, and it proposes no new module.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the instrument §3's done-when binds to, docs/research/data/crew-contract-baseline/measure.py, re-implements transcript indexing and per-request token accounting that reckon/velocity.py already owns.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §2 is itself a reuse map (every binding sentence must name the refusal or check that enforces it) and §3 cites the mechanisms it must not break, tests/test_skill_contract_parity.py and docs/research/data/crew-contract-baseline/measure.py; the one owner its search did not reach is the transcript-usage reader, reported below.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the references are a layer over the runtime prompt in reckon/crew/prompts.py, but §3 scopes them to a coordinator composing a delegation by hand and tests/test_skill_contract_parity.py derives its expectations from the prompt's own strings, so the two surfaces are compared rather than asserted independently and the layer carries a stated reason.
